        10                      SENATOR COOK:  Mr. President,

        11       this bill permits a school district to charge

        12       tuition for students who are residing in tax

        13       exempt properties.

        14                      With the problems that we have of

        15       trying to fund schools adequately, when we have

        16       large establishments within school districts

        17       which are sending substantial numbers of

        18       students to the school district and are

        19       contributing absolutely nothing toward the cost

        20       of educating those students, it simply shifts

        21       the burden to everybody else who resides there.

        22                      In one particular school

        23       district, the assessed value of that particular

        24       property is over $1 million that is off the tax

        25       rolls.  Conversely, there are 30 students







                                                             
1540

         1       attending school -- the Fallsburg School from

         2       one particular property at a cost of at least

         3       $100,000 per year to all the other taxpayers in

         4       the school district and those students are

         5       contributing absolutely nothing toward the cost

         6       of their education and the property is

         7       contributing nothing toward the general budget

         8       of the school district.

         9                      So this is an attempt to remedy

        10       that situation by permitting the school district

        11       to charge tuition to those students who reside

        12       in that type of property.

        14       Paterson.

        16       President.

        24       public policy of trying to make sure that any

        25       students that use our public schools share in

         1       the cost, or at least that their families share

         2       in the cost and that with the difficulty funding

         3       schools, that large sums of money that would be

         4       not operable because individuals are living on

         5       poverty that's not taxed is -- would be a

         6       significant issue.

         7                      My question to you is do you see

         8       this legislation as the only remedy?  Wouldn't

         9       an impact fee or some kind of use tax that might

        10       be applied more to the entity, not to the

        11       individuals who are using the school, achieve

        12       the same purpose and not in any way penalize

        13       children from getting their education?

        11       two don't seem to meet the approval of the

        12       members of the Legislature for -- or at least

        18       taxpayers in the district where the property

        19       taxes continue to escalate are paying the cost
